claims: A clean CodeRabbit run probably never counts as `reviewed`, so every clean PR gets a wasted manual review — `scripts/pr/pr-ready-state-core.mjs:762`: `classifyCodeRabbitReviewSignal` only returns `reviewed` for a PR review whose body contains `**Run ID**`; closeout posts `@coderabbitai review` for a head CodeRabbit already reviewed, spending a Pro+ review, and state stays `requested` for good
The tests only cover a body with actionable comments (`pr-ready-state.test.mjs:2226`)

The closeout can report all-clear while the review it just requested is still running — `.agents/skills/babysit-pr/SKILL.md:295-316` (same text in `.claude/skills/...` and `docs/notes/pr-ready-state.md:123-127, 399-402`): CodeRabbit's inline comments become unresolved threads and unreplied root comments that hit required gates, so a PR can be reported clear and then turn not-ready

Minor: request comments aren't filtered by author — `scripts/pr/pr-ready-state-core.mjs:772-784`: any commenter, including a fork contributor, posting `@coderabbitai review` with the head marker flips the state to `requested` and suppresses the closeout for that head
The Codex request detection has the same gap (request comments not filtered by author)

judge_reasoning.3829654081: The review never raises the file growing past the line cap or the need to split pr-ready-state-core.mjs.
judge_reasoning.3829659544: The review does not mention that the sample JSON in docs/notes/pr-ready-state.md lacks codeRabbitReviewSignal.
judge_reasoning.3829659546: Finding 2 says the procedure posts the request before the pair and then fails to wait for the requested review. That is a different problem from sites running the projection pair before the closeout rule.
judge_reasoning.3829659550: The review does not flag the fallbacks when currentHeadOid is null (timestamp matching, or accepting any marked request).
judge_reasoning.3830259678: Finding 3 says request comments aren't filtered by author, so any commenter, including a fork contributor, can flip the state to requested and suppress closeout. That is the same defect.

1.why: classifyCodeRabbitReviewSignal (core.mjs:760-770) only returns `reviewed` when a CodeRabbit PR review body matches `**Run ID**`. It never reads CodeRabbit's issue comments. The repo's own PR #1918 fixture (pr-feedback-state.test.mjs:3360-3373) shows a clean run's 'No actionable comments were generated' result landing in the walkthrough issue comment. So a clean head reads as missing or stale, which triggers the manual request, and the gate then stays `requested`.

2.why: Only the first test (pr-ready-state.test.mjs:2226-2230) uses an 'Actionable comments posted: 1' body. The summarizeReadyState test at :2274 uses a body that contains only the Run ID line, so the tests don't only cover bodies with actionable comments.

3.why: This is the all-clear-while-the-requested-review-is-still-running gap in docs/notes/pr-ready-state.md steps 8-10 (lines 399-408). The known defect at docs/notes/pr-ready-state.md:408 (Functional Correctness, Major) already covers it, and the SKILL.md text mirrors it.

4.why: It's true that the issue-comment loop at core.mjs:772-784 never checks the author. This is the known defect 'scripts/pr/pr-ready-state-core.mjs:772 Trust only authorized closeout requests'.

5.why: classifyCodexReviewSignal (core.mjs:707-730) is existing code that this diff doesn't touch; the diff only adds the CodeRabbit functions. The claim gives no location or impact, so it isn't a defect in this change.
